A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPE-BR pricing research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite reformatting and the addition of Appendix L.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations of demand estimation, Nash-equilibrium convergence and regret in Section 6 and Appendix J, including Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v4 retains those simulations and adds original shape-parameter sensitivity results in Appendix J.3 and Figure 8.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations (10)–(12) retain normalized linear least-squares estimation, a separate monotone s-concave link fit, and subsequent best-response pricing. The new sensitivity experiment varies an existing parameter without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains synthetic sequential pricing with Gaussian-CDF demand links and markets of 2, 4 or 6 sellers. Shape-parameter misspecification changes estimator settings within this coverage. Appendix L's additional distributions are mathematical examples, not evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally compares SPE-BR against external pricing or estimation methods. The added shape-parameter variants are settings of the same algorithm, rather than new comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix J.3 adds a sensitivity protocol fixing N=4 and beta_i=0.9 while sweeping assumed shape parameters through -0.2, -0.1, 0, 0.1 and 0.2. The previously reported experiments retain their sampling distributions, exploration schedules and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: v4 adds an analysis of how misspecifying s_i affects estimation, equilibrium convergence and regret in Appendix J.3/Figure 8. The contraction-regime analysis and unequal-exploration robustness experiment already present in v3 are retained as J.1 and J.2.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 30 independent simulation repetitions and 95% confidence intervals. The added experiment follows the existing setup and uncertainty-display practice; no changed run count, significance test or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figures 5–7 retain their results. New Figure 8 reports equilibrium-convergence slopes ranging from -0.37 to -0.26 and regret slopes from 0.49 to 0.57 across the five shape settings. These are additional results under a new configuration, not improvements over matched v3 results.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.3 is narrowed from existence and uniqueness to existence, with uniqueness added explicitly under contraction in Lemma 3.7. Appendix G exposes shape-dependent constants and adds a misspecification argument. New Appendix L substantially expands the mathematics through optimal-concavity definitions, product properties, density/CDF/survival-function propositions and proofs. The headline regret and convergence exponents remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 2.1 retain the same semiparametric pricing, shape-constrained estimation and concentration contributions. The headline T^(5/7) regret and T^(-1/7) equilibrium-convergence claims, with their stated dimensional and logarithmic factors, are unchanged.

C2.justification: Remark 4.3 explicitly limits optimality to the derived upper bound and disclaims minimax optimality. v4 also clarifies negative cross-price effects and the role of elliptical exploration, discusses conservative versus overly restrictive shape choices, and attributes the new experiment's slope differences to finite-sample variation.

D1.justification: v4 adds guidance on obtaining demand bounds from historical sales and capacity limits, and documents the new sensitivity experiment's parameter choices in J.3. The solver description and supplementary ZIP/notebook access instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Remark D.2 adds Luo et al. (2024) to contextualize randomized exploration designs. Appendix L expands discussion of the already cited Bagnoli and Bergstrom (2006), including reproduced distribution summaries. The central positioning relative to linear pricing and single-index estimation remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 reorganizes Section 3 around Main Assumptions, converts the regret/equilibrium subsections into paragraph headings, and removes the Step 1–3 framing. It expands selected explanations and adds an LLM-usage disclosure, while retaining most existing prose and the overall narrative.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively retypeset with different typography, narrower text blocks, a compact grouped author block, compressed equations and resized or repositioned figures. v4 adds robustness Figure 8 and distribution-table Figures 10–11; v3's algorithm illustration remains as Figure 9.

improvement.justification: v4 improves precision by correcting the strong-concavity-only uniqueness statement, qualifying optimality and adding a bounded robustness check. However, new Appendix L introduces substantive reliability problems: its Pareto/lognormal discussion contradicts Figure 11, and the power-function example in L.3.4 violates its own displayed curvature condition. These benefits and new mathematical errors leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
